alex.m: quick question — where's the canonical place to look for p50/p95/p99 + TTFT + tokens/sec for model endpoints? i'm tuning alerts and want to avoid duplicate dashboards :slightly_smiling_face:

julia: for latency percentiles we mostly use the 'model-serving-latency' Grafana dashboard (team:eng-platform). it has p50/p95/p99 by route and model_version. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/model-serving-latency

kevin: TTFT (time-to-first-token) isn't always instrumented as a separate metric, but we derive it from the histogram `inference_latency_seconds` by splitting first-byte and rest. prefer this prom metric: `inference_first_byte_seconds` if available. Tempo traces also show it per-request.

alex.m: do you have the PromQL snippets?

julia: yep — quick ones below. note: replace `job`/`route` labels with your service name.

julia: ```
# p95 request latency (seconds)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model))

# TTFT (derived first byte) if we have first-byte gauge
rate(inference_first_byte_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(inference_first_byte_seconds_count[5m])

# tokens/sec per model (summed)
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model)
```

kevin: if your service doesn't emit `inference_first_byte_seconds`, fall back to trace-based TTFT from Tempo: query traces where span.name contains `first_byte` and aggregate duration. link: https://tempo.redwood.internal/explore

alex.m: where are logs for correlating slow requests? need to join traces -> logs to see model version & prompt size.

kevin: Loki is our logs store. search example:

kevin: ```
{job="model-serving"} |= "inference_start" |= "request_id=123" | json | line_format "${request_id} ${model_version} ${prompt_tokens} ${duration_ms}"
```

julia: recommendation for alert tuning:
- alert on sustained p95/p99 CPU or latency increases over 10m window, not single spikes
- use `for: 5m` on PagerDuty alerts, `for: 1m` on SLO dashboards only
- group by `model` and `route` so a noisy model doesn't blow up global alerts

alex.m: any existing alerts i should copy?

observability-bot: there is an alert template: `Alert: ServiceLatencyHigh` in repo `infra/alerts/model-serving-alerts.yaml`. See: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/alerts/model-serving-alerts.yaml

kevin: specifics we use currently: p95 > 800ms for 'fast' routes triggers a warning, p99 > 2.5s triggers page. for high-throughput endpoints we look at tokens/sec drop as an early signal of throttling.

alex.m: curious — how do we compute tokens/sec per request vs overall throughput?

julia: tokens/sec per-request is computed at request end: `prompt_tokens + generated_tokens` divided by (response_end - response_start). Overall throughput is just `sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m]))`. both are exposed on the dashboard.

alex.m: thanks. last thing — is there a quick checklist for lowering noisy alerts?

kevin: short checklist:
1) ensure alert groups by model and route
2) set appropriate `for` windows (10m for p95 trending)
3) add suppression during deploy windows (use label `deploying=true`)
4) tie critical alerts to SRE runbook and include `trace_id`/`request_id` in alert payload
5) use burn rate for SLO-based paging instead of simple p99 thresholds when load fluctuates

alex.m: perfect. i'll copy the PromQL and open a PR to add a TTFT panel to my team's dashboard. pinging @sre-oncall for any gotchas during dashboard edits.

sre-oncall: FYI when you add panels, avoid heavy PromQL with long aggregations on the dashboard default refresh. use 5m query windows and pre-aggregated recording rules where possible. happy to review the PR. :thumbsup:

alex.m: awesome — i'll post the PR link here once up. thanks all! :rocket:
